title: Finish the Magic Square

concept.title: Test every row, column and diagonal as soon as it is full
body: A 3 by 3 **magic square** uses each of the digits 1 to 9 exactly once, and each row, each column and both diagonals add up to 15. Some cells are already given (a `0` means an empty cell). Count the ways to fill the empty cells with the unused digits to get a magic square.

The search fills the empty cells in reading order with digits not used yet. Trying all `9!` fillings and checking at the end would be slow and silly: instead, **after each placement** check every line (three cells) whose cells are all filled, and reject the placement as soon as such a line does not add up to 15.
The empty board has exactly 8 solutions (the rotations and mirror images of one square). Checking a line early cuts most of the 362880 fillings away.

statement: A 3 by 3 board contains some of the digits 1 to 9 (all different); an empty cell is written as `0`. Fill the empty cells with the digits that are not used yet, so that the digits 1 to 9 each appear exactly once and every row, every column and both diagonals have the sum 15. Count the ways.
inputFormat: 3 lines with 3 characters each: the digits 0 to 9 without spaces.
constraints: The nonzero digits on the board are different.

examples.note: A magic square with the 8 in the top left corner: the rotations and mirrors give 2 such squares (the middle is always 5).

hints: Remember which digits are used; the given digits are used from the start.
After placing a digit, check each line that is completely filled: its sum must be 15.
The cells given at the start also take part in the line checks.

starter.python:
board = [input().strip() for _ in range(3)]

explanation: The empty cells are filled in reading order with unused digits. After each placement every completely filled line must add to 15, otherwise the digit is rejected. At the end of the board the lines are checked once more (the given cells may form a full line).
solution.complexity: Time tiny (far fewer than 9! nodes), space O(1).
